judged_text: The Salesforce connection path now eagerly refreshes the token and overwrites `credential.key` on every service instantiation, and in sharing mode parseRefreshTokenResponse's minimum schema strips the Salesforce response down to `{access_token}`, so the persisted key becomes just `{access_token, refresh_token}`. Every Salesforce calendar operation now performs an extra OAuth roundtrip plus a credential write, and a transient refresh failure throws (HttpError / rejected connection promise) where the previous constructor proceeded on the stored access token, failing the whole operation; in sharing mode the overwrite permanently drops `instance_url`, `id`, `signature`, and `token_type` from the stored credential, so the next instantiation builds the jsforce connection with an undefined instanceUrl and every subsequent Salesforce call fails.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs a refresh-token request immediately during service initialization (it `fetch`es the Salesforce token endpoint and then `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning a `jsforce.Connection`). This means every instantiation triggers an extra OAuth roundtrip and a DB write regardless of whether the stored access token is still valid, and a transient refresh failure now throws/rejects early (`if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw ...`). Additionally, the refresh parsing path uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`, which in “sharing mode” (when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set) validates against `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`) rather than the Salesforce schema, and because it’s a `z.object(...)` without `.passthrough()`, it will drop fields not declared in the minimum schema. The subsequent credential write persists only the parsed fields plus the old `refresh_token` (`data: { key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token } }`), so important Salesforce fields like `instance_url` can be lost from `credential.key` if they are not part of the minimum schema, causing follow-on breakage wherever those fields are required.
